item.title: When is Sweden's parliament set to vote on new migration laws?
item.description: Sweden's government is currently racing to get some of the most important laws in its "paradigm shift on migration" passed by parliament before September's election. Here are the dates when key votes are scheduled.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Two thirds of Tidö Agreement fulfilled, Swedish politicians laud Ukraine on four-year anniversary, and more news from Sweden on Wednesday.

item.title: 'No ETA, no entry': UK imposes tighter travel rules for Europeans
item.description: The UK government has warned European travellers that they will be refused entry from February 25th if they do not have the required ETA visa waiver - while British dual nationals will be required to use a UK passport.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: rea
item.description: This week marks the start of Sweden's annual book sale. But where does the Swedish word for sale come from?

item.title: UPDATED: What does Sweden's plan to restrict benefits for newcomers mean for work permit holders?
item.description: Sweden is pushing forward with new rules which will make it harder for foreigners to qualify for social insurance, including parental benefits and child support, with the government set to publish a draft bill proposing tougher rules.

item.title: New: The Local’s self-paced Swedish course
item.description: Due to a popular demand The Local's self-paced online Swedish course for beginners is back, designed to make learning flexible and practical.

item.title: Swedish employer organisations warn of teen deportation 'brain drain'
item.description: A number of Swedish employer organisations have warned that the deportation of teenage children of work permit holders risks causing a “brain drain” of highly-skilled workers.

item.title: Work permits, Mello, and marzipan: What changes in Sweden in March 2026
item.description: Parliament will vote on hiking the minimum salary for a work permit and Sweden's Eurovision contender will be chosen. Here's what happens in Sweden in March.

item.title: Sweden's teen deportations: 'It feels like they wanted him to turn 18 so they could reject him'
item.description: This week’s episode of Sweden in Focus Extra features an interview with the parents of a student facing deportation from Sweden.

item.title: Sweden's Migration Minister wants to solve teen deportation problem 'this year'
item.description: Sweden's Migration Minister Johan Forssell has said he hopes to solve the teen deportation problem "as soon as possible", telling reporters he does not have to wait until a new law with an exemption clause is scheduled to come into force next January.
